course.title: PMP® Exam Preparation and Business Application
course.audience: PMP candidates, project managers, program and PMO professionals, product and transformation leaders, military and government project leaders, and business professionals responsible for delivering measurable project outcomes
course.description: A 35-hour independent, AI-native Obserra Academy course aligned to the July 2026 Project Management Professional (PMP) Examination Content Outline. The course combines original exam preparation, predictive, adaptive and hybrid project practices, documented public project cases, business application exercises, original practice questions, a full readiness plan, and a governed course-specific AI tutor. It does not reproduce PMI official courseware, copyrighted examination questions, exam dumps, or proprietary test banks and does not imply PMI sponsorship or endorsement.
course.sourceOfTruth: Project Management Professional (PMP) Examination Content Outline - July 2026, verified 2026-08-06
prerequisites: No PMP certification is required to begin the course.
Learners seeking PMP certification remain responsible for satisfying PMI education, experience, application, audit, examination, and conduct requirements.
Access to the current PMBOK® Guide and other PMI-recommended references is strongly recommended and may require separate purchase or membership access.
Learners must acknowledge the Obserra informational-use disclaimer, intellectual-property restrictions, and assessment-integrity rules before accessing paid course content.
outcomes: Explain the July 2026 PMP exam structure, eligibility pathways, domain weights, delivery-approach distribution, and assessment expectations using current PMI sources.
Apply the People domain tasks through leadership, conflict, stakeholder, communication, knowledge-transfer, and team scenarios.
Apply the Process domain tasks through integrated planning, tailoring, scope, value, resources, procurement, finance, quality, schedule, status, and closure decisions.
Apply the Business Environment domain tasks through governance, compliance, change, impediment, risk, continuous-improvement, organizational-change, and external-environment scenarios.
Select and tailor predictive, adaptive or agile, and hybrid approaches based on value, uncertainty, complexity, risk, governance, and stakeholder needs.
Interpret project facts, metrics, assumptions, confidence, limitations, and trade-offs without relying on memorized terminology alone.
Use original exam-style scenarios to identify the strongest next action, the accountable role, the relevant evidence, and the governing principle.
Translate project management practices into practical artifacts and decisions for technology, cybersecurity, healthcare, government, operations, product, and enterprise transformation environments.
Build a personalized study plan using domain performance, practice-question rationale, retrieval practice, spaced review, and targeted remediation.
Demonstrate professional responsibility, respect, fairness, honesty, and assessment integrity throughout the course.

examAlignment.trainingHoursClaim: Designed as 35 hours of self-paced project-management instruction aligned to the July 2026 PMP Examination Content Outline. PMI alone determines certification eligibility and may audit or reject training.

modules.title: PMP Exam Architecture and Modern Project Leadership
modules.description: Establish the current exam, eligibility, ethics, learning strategy, project-value orientation, and predictive, adaptive and hybrid context before domain-level study.

lessons.title: PMP Eligibility, Application, Audit, and Exam Experience
lessons.description: Use current PMI sources to understand education and experience pathways, the 35-hour training requirement, application evidence, audit exposure, the 180-question exam, and the 240-minute testing window.
objectives: Determine which eligibility pathway may apply
Avoid double counting overlapping project experience

lessons.title: The 2026 Exam Content Outline: Domains, Tasks, and Enablers
lessons.description: Map People, Process, and Business Environment tasks to realistic project decisions and distinguish the ECO from the PMBOK Guide.
objectives: Describe how tasks and enablers guide preparation
Build a personal domain coverage map

lessons.title: From Scope, Schedule, and Cost to Value and Outcomes
lessons.description: Examine why modern project success includes stakeholder value, desired outcomes, benefits, ethics, resilience, and business impact in addition to traditional constraints.
objectives: Recognize when delivery is on plan but not creating value

lessons.title: Predictive, Adaptive, and Hybrid Thinking with Professional Ethics
lessons.description: Select a delivery approach based on uncertainty, value cadence, governance, technical risk, and stakeholder needs while applying professional responsibility, respect, fairness, and honesty.
objectives: Explain why the strongest exam answer protects value and accountability

modules.title: People Domain I: Vision, Leadership, and Team Performance
modules.description: Build the leadership and team judgment needed to develop a common vision, lead diverse teams, establish roles, empower people, and solve performance problems.

lessons.title: Develop and Sustain a Common Vision
lessons.description: Translate business intent into a shared project vision and diagnose misunderstandings before they become delivery failures.
objectives: Keep vision current as conditions change

lessons.title: Leadership Styles, Authority, and Situational Judgment
lessons.description: Select coaching, facilitating, directing, serving, and delegating behaviors based on competence, urgency, risk, autonomy, and team context.
objectives: Avoid command-and-control reflexes in adaptive environments

lessons.title: Roles, Responsibilities, Empowerment, and Accountability
lessons.description: Clarify ownership and decision rights without undermining team autonomy or creating unaccountable work.

lessons.title: Team Diversity, Trust, Psychological Safety, and Performance
lessons.description: Use varied skills and perspectives, surface dissent, and create conditions for early risk reporting and constructive challenge.
objectives: Use team diversity as a decision-quality control

lessons.title: Performance Coaching and Structured Problem Solving
lessons.description: Separate system problems, capability gaps, role ambiguity, behavioral concerns, and unrealistic constraints before choosing an intervention.
objectives: Escalate proportionately when risk exceeds authority

modules.title: People Domain II: Stakeholders, Conflict, Communication, and Knowledge
modules.description: Apply stakeholder analysis, conflict resolution, expectation management, communication planning, reporting, feedback, and knowledge transfer.

lessons.title: Stakeholder Identification, Analysis, and Engagement
lessons.description: Identify formal and informal stakeholders, analyze influence and impact, and tailor engagement to project objectives and stakeholder needs.

lessons.title: Align and Manage Stakeholder and Customer Expectations
lessons.description: Facilitate expectation alignment, preserve trust, monitor satisfaction, and respond when desired outcomes conflict.
objectives: Respond to changing customer needs without bypassing governance

lessons.title: Conflict Sources, Resolution Strategies, and Ground Rules
lessons.description: Diagnose conflict context and use collaboration, compromise, accommodation, avoidance, or direction deliberately rather than reflexively.
objectives: Restore ground rules and working relationships

lessons.title: Communication, Reporting, Feedback, and Knowledge Transfer
lessons.description: Create communication strategies, reporting artifacts, feedback loops, and knowledge-transfer mechanisms that support decisions and continuity.
objectives: Preserve knowledge during transitions and closure

modules.title: Process Domain I: Tailoring, Integration, Scope, and Value
modules.description: Integrate plans and delivery, tailor methods, define scope, prioritize value, estimate work, manage dependencies, and use data for decisions.

lessons.title: Assess Complexity and Tailor the Development Approach
lessons.description: Assess uncertainty, complexity, stakeholder access, compliance, technology, value cadence, and organizational constraints to recommend predictive, adaptive, or hybrid delivery.

lessons.title: Build and Maintain an Integrated Project Management Plan
lessons.description: Connect scope, schedule, cost, resources, quality, risk, procurement, communications, governance, compliance, and benefits into a coherent decision system.
objectives: Maintain the plan as conditions change

lessons.title: Scope, Requirements, Backlogs, and Work Decomposition
lessons.description: Define and obtain agreement on scope, decompose work, manage requirements and backlogs, and recognize gold plating and uncontrolled expansion.

lessons.title: Value-Based Delivery, Benefits, and Incremental Outcomes
lessons.description: Prioritize work using stakeholder value, assess opportunities for incremental delivery, and verify that benefits measurement exists.
objectives: Connect project outputs to measurable benefits

lessons.title: Estimation, Dependencies, Assumptions, and Data-Informed Decisions
lessons.description: Estimate effort and resources, expose assumptions, analyze dependencies, and use data without creating false precision.

modules.title: Process Domain II: Resources, Procurement, Finance, and Quality
modules.description: Plan and optimize resources, procurement, suppliers, contracts, project finance, reserves, quality, regulatory needs, and continuous improvement.

lessons.title: Resource Planning, Capacity, Availability, and Optimization
lessons.description: Plan people, equipment, facilities, services, and specialized capability while resolving shortages and competing priorities.

lessons.title: Procurement Strategy, Contract Types, Negotiation, and Supplier Performance
lessons.description: Select procurement strategies and contract structures based on scope clarity, risk allocation, market conditions, incentives, performance, and governance.

lessons.title: Project Finance, Contingency, Reserves, Forecasting, and Cost Control
lessons.description: Analyze financial needs, quantify contingency, plan spend tracking and reporting, monitor variance, and manage reserves through governance.

lessons.title: Quality Planning, Regulatory Compliance, Cost of Quality, and Improvement
lessons.description: Translate quality requirements into processes and acceptance evidence, account for regulatory obligations, manage cost of quality, and improve continuously.
objectives: Evaluate prevention appraisal and failure costs

modules.title: Process Domain III: Schedule, Status, Artifacts, and Closure
modules.description: Build and control schedules, evaluate status, manage artifacts, communicate performance, transition deliverables, and close projects or phases responsibly.

lessons.title: Schedule Networks, Dependencies, Critical Path, and Baselines
lessons.description: Create an integrated schedule, understand logic and dependencies, identify critical path, baseline the plan, and distinguish dates from evidence-based forecasts.

lessons.title: Schedule Risk, Variance, Forecasting, and Recovery Options
lessons.description: Analyze variance, model uncertainty, assess compression options, and communicate recovery trade-offs without hiding risk.
objectives: Compare crashing and fast tracking risks

lessons.title: Project Metrics, Status, Forecasts, and Artifact Management
lessons.description: Choose decision-useful metrics, reconcile conflicting data, tailor artifacts, preserve accessibility, and communicate facts, forecasts, confidence, and limitations.

lessons.title: Transition, Acceptance, Closure, Retrospectives, and Knowledge Retention
lessons.description: Verify acceptance and operational readiness, conclude contractual and financial work, release resources, preserve knowledge, and close without abandoning unresolved risk.

modules.title: Business Environment I: Governance, Compliance, and Change
modules.description: Establish governance and success metrics, plan compliance, execute change control, support organizational change, and respond to external business conditions.

lessons.title: Project Governance, Ethics, Escalation, and Success Metrics
lessons.description: Define decision rights, rules, policies, reporting, ethics, success measures, and escalation thresholds appropriate to the project and enterprise.
objectives: Connect governance to value and accountability

lessons.title: Compliance Categories, Requirements, Evidence, and Consequences
lessons.description: Identify security, privacy, health and safety, sustainability, contractual, industry, and regulatory requirements and plan proportionate evidence and response.
objectives: Measure compliance without unsupported certification claims

lessons.title: Integrated Change Control and Configuration Integrity
lessons.description: Evaluate change requests, analyze impact, obtain authority, update baselines and artifacts, and communicate decisions across predictive and adaptive environments.

lessons.title: Organizational Change and the External Business Environment
lessons.description: Assess culture and adoption needs while monitoring regulatory, technological, geopolitical, market, and sustainability changes that affect scope, backlog, value, or risk.
objectives: Adapt project direction without losing governance

modules.title: Business Environment II: Risk, Impediments, Improvement, and Exam Readiness
modules.description: Manage risk and issues, remove impediments, improve continuously, govern AI and sustainability concerns, and convert knowledge into a disciplined exam and workplace action plan.

lessons.title: Risk Identification, Analysis, Response, Monitoring, and Communication
lessons.description: Build and maintain risk information, distinguish threats and opportunities, select responses, monitor exposure, and communicate residual risk.
objectives: Communicate risk status and residual exposure

lessons.title: Issues, Impediments, Root Causes, and Intervention Strategies
lessons.description: Recognize when risk becomes an issue, evaluate impact, prioritize blockers, collaborate with stakeholders, and reassess interventions.
objectives: Escalate when authority or impact requires it

lessons.title: Continuous Improvement, Lessons Learned, and Organizational Process Assets
lessons.description: Turn retrospectives, data, defects, outcomes, and lessons learned into updated practices rather than archived documents.

lessons.title: AI, Sustainability, Security, and Modern Project Risk
lessons.description: Evaluate AI-supported project decisions, sustainability information, cybersecurity exposure, model limitations, human oversight, and compliance in modern projects.
objectives: Integrate sustainability and security into planning and governance

lessons.title: Exam Strategy, Original Simulation, Remediation, and Business Application Capstone
lessons.description: Apply a repeatable decision method to original exam-style scenarios, analyze distractors, manage time, complete the final assessment, and produce a 30-day readiness and workplace application plan.
objectives: Build a targeted exam and business-application plan
